doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Listening to the Ellington band and its records
summary: Williams and Peterson recall Ellington band members and records; Bellson found no drum parts and Duke trusted his musical intelligence.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Oh yes he could play that thing. He used to love that thing. But Ben Webster, that was another case of — I think that we were so blessed to come through the time when we had those people to listen to, to appreciate, and just to make us lose ourselves in what they did. Because they were capable. Ellington — I’d get lost in his beauty, the beauty of the chords, the beauty of the way they and played together, the way they would breathe together, and the sound that they made from Otto Hardwicke to all of the guys.
Oh, Hodges, of course, you know and the baritone player, don’t forget that, he was a baby when he joined the band I understand, from Boston — I can’t think of his name.
Harry Carney, yeah. And Ben Webster when he got in there. My first record, the first record I bought was “KoKo.” And the second was “Truckin.’” And then “Cottontail.”
